title: Antioxidant Peptides from Skipjack tuna: Ameliorate Function on Cigarette Smoke Extract-Induced COPD in Cell Model by Targeting Oxidative Stress, Inflammation and Apoptosis.
authors: Zeng, Yu-Hui; Jin, Yang-Yan; Sheng, Yan; Chi, Chang-Feng; Wang, Bin
one_liner_zh: 研究金枪鱼抗氧化肽对香烟烟雾提取物诱导的COPD细胞模型的保护作用，涉及Keap1-Nrf2等信号通路，但核心是蛋白-小肽互作而非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Antioxidant peptides show significant activity and can be developed into functional foods for treating chronic diseases. Cigarette smoke components can cause damage or even apoptosis of lung cells, eventually leading to chronic lung diseases. Therefore, this study aimed to investigate the protective effects and mechanisms of Skipjack tuna peptides against in vitro cigarette smoke extract (CSE)-induced chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). The results demonstrated that tuna peptides DVGRG (S1), PHPR (S5), GRVPR (S6), and SVTEV (S7) significantly enhanced the activities of SOD, CAT, and GSH-Px by upregulating the mRNA transcription levels of Keap1 and Nrf2, consequently reducing ROS and MDA levels in CSE-induced COPD model of MLE-12 cells. Molecular docking analysis revealed that S1, S6, and S7 competitively inhibited the Keap1-Nrf2 interaction by binding to the Kelch domain of Keap1, whereas S5 operated through a non-competitive mechanism. These peptides also downregulated p65 mRNA expression and upregulated IkappaBalpha mRNA expression, leading to a significant reduction in inflammatory cytokines of IL-1beta, IL-6, and TNF-alpha, thereby alleviating inflammatory responses. Furthermore, these peptides significantly inhibited CSE-induced apoptosis by restoring mitochondrial membrane potential and upregulating the Bcl-2/Bax ratio. Additionally, S1, S5, S6, and S7 promoted MLE-12 cell migration in a concentration-dependent manner, suggesting a role in lung epithelial repair and regeneration. In conclusion, tuna peptides S1, S5, S6, and S7 exert antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, anti-apoptotic, and cell migration-promoting effects through the regulation of the Keap1/Nrf2 and NF-kappaB signaling pathways, as well as Bcl-2/Bax apoptotic balance, providing a promising strategy for mitigating CSE-induced lung injury.
abstract_zh: 抗氧化肽显示出显著活性，可开发为治疗慢性疾病的功能性食品。香烟烟雾成分可导致肺细胞损伤甚至凋亡，最终引发慢性肺部疾病。因此，本研究旨在探讨鲣鱼肽对体外香烟烟雾提取物（CSE）诱导的慢性阻塞性肺疾病（COPD）的保护作用及其机制。结果表明，金枪鱼肽DVGRG（S1）、PHPR（S5）、GRVPR（S6）和SVTEV（S7）通过上调Keap1和Nrf2的mRNA转录水平，显著增强SOD、CAT和GSH-Px的活性，从而降低CSE诱导的COPD模型MLE-12细胞中ROS和MDA水平。分子对接分析显示，S1、S6和S7通过与Keap1的Kelch结构域结合，竞争性抑制Keap1-Nrf2相互作用，而S5则通过非竞争性机制发挥作用。这些肽还下调p65 mRNA表达并上调IkappaBalpha mRNA表达，导致IL-1beta、IL-6和TNF-alpha等炎症细胞因子显著减少，从而缓解炎症反应。此外，这些肽通过恢复线粒体膜电位和上调Bcl-2/Bax比值，显著抑制CSE诱导的细胞凋亡。另外，S1、S5、S6和S7以浓度依赖性方式促进MLE-12细胞迁移，提示其在肺上皮修复和再生中发挥作用。总之，金枪鱼肽S1、S5、S6和S7通过调节Keap1/Nrf2和NF-kappaB信号通路以及Bcl-2/Bax凋亡平衡，发挥抗氧化、抗炎、抗凋亡和促进细胞迁移的作用，为减轻CSE诱导的肺损伤提供了有前景的策略。
